scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation at Walmart. Let me start by going through what happened step by step. First, I'm a 24-year-old male working at Walmart for the summer. My job is mainly in the back room dealing with inventory, which includes lifting heavy boxes. One of my co-workers is a woman in her early to mid-30s, who seems physically fit and doesn't have any obvious disabilities. She approached me and asked for help lifting a heavy box. I agreed, thinking we'd do a team lift. But when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me instead of helping. I asked if she was ready, and she said it just needed to go into a bin that's about 4 feet high. I offered to help, but she said it was too heavy for her and asked me to lift it into the bin alone. I told her I was happy to help if she was having trouble, but I wasn't going to lift all her heavy boxes while she watched. She got upset and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team talked to me about it, saying that when someone asks for help, I should help them because that's part of being a team. I explained what happened, clarifying that she didn't actually help and just wanted me to do all the work. I also mentioned that both of us are paid to do the same job, and if she couldn't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. I added that I wasn't the designated heavy lifter and suggested discussing it further with HR if needed. Then I stormed off, feeling annoyed. So, was I the asshole here? It seems like two people (the co-worker and the head guy) are against me. But I feel like I was just trying to stand up for myself and not be taken advantage of. Let me think about this from different angles. On one hand, teamwork is important, and helping out a co-worker when they ask seems like the right thing to do. But on the other hand, I was expecting a team effort, not just doing all the work while she watched. Maybe I should have been more understanding and just lifted the box for her, even if it meant doing more work. But then again, if everyone expects me to do all the heavy lifting, that's not fair either. I also wonder if there's a gender dynamic here. She's a woman asking a man for help with heavy lifting, which might be a common occurrence. Maybe she's used to men helping her without expecting her to help in return. But I was hoping for a more equal partnership. Another thing to consider is the workplace culture. The head guy emphasized teamwork, so maybe the expectation is that we help each other out regardless of the situation. But I felt like I was being taken advantage of, which made me upset. I also need to think about how I responded. I told her I wasn't going to lift all her boxes, which might have come off as confrontational. Maybe I could have handled it more diplomatically, like suggesting we work together instead of doing it alone. In the end, I feel like I was trying to set boundaries to ensure fairness, but maybe I went about it the wrong way. It's possible that I could have been more accommodating without feeling like I was being taken advantage of. However, I also don't want to be the one always doing the heavy lifting while others watch. So, was I the asshole? I'm not entirely sure, but I think there's room for improvement in how I handled the situation. Maybe I could have communicated my feelings more clearly and worked towards a solution that benefits both of us.
